label: Army is raiding
summary: Whether the army is currently out raiding.
details: A raid that has been interrupted by a fight still counts as a raid. Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Army is besieging
summary: Whether the army is currently taking part in a siege.
details: A siege that has been interrupted by a fight still counts. Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Siege relevant for
summary: Whether the army is in a siege that matters to the given character.
details: The character is written as the value, for example `scope:character`. The game does not say what counts as relevant; vanilla only ever passes `root`.

label: Is at home
summary: Whether the character is at home.
details: The game does not say what counts as home here. Write `yes` to require it.

label: Is in province
summary: Whether the character is currently in the given province.
details: The province is written as the value. Vanilla uses it with a barony's province, for example `scope:barony.title_province`.

label: Same province as
summary: Whether the character is in the same province as the given character.
details: The other character is written as the value, for example `root` or `scope:mother`.

label: At war
summary: Whether the character is at war.
details: Only the character's own wars count. Wars that their lieges (the rulers above them) are fighting are not considered. Write `yes` to require a war, `no` to require peace.

label: At war as attacker
summary: Whether the character is at war on the attacking side.
details: Only the character's own wars count, not wars of their lieges (the rulers above them).

label: At war as defender
summary: Whether the character is at war on the defending side.
details: Only the character's own wars count, not wars of their lieges (the rulers above them).

label: At war with
summary: Whether the character is at war with the given character.
details: The other character is written as the value, for example `scope:recipient` or `root`. Only the character's own wars count, not wars of their lieges (the rulers above them).

label: At war with liege
summary: Whether the character is at war with their own liege (the ruler directly above them).
details: Vanilla only uses it with `no`.

label: Is attacker in war
summary: Whether the given character is on the attacking side of this war.
details: It runs on a war. The character to check is written as the value, for example `scope:actor` or `root`.

label: Attacker in war
summary: Whether the character is on the attacking side of the given war.
details: The war is written as the value, for example `scope:war`. It is the reverse of `is_attacker`, which runs on the war and names the character.

label: Attracted to gender of
summary: Whether the character's sexuality makes them attracted to the given character's gender.
details: The other character is written as the value, for example `root`.

label: Attracted to men
summary: Whether the character is attracted to men.
details: Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Attracted to women
summary: Whether the character is attracted to women.
details: Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Is available
summary: Checks several availability conditions of a character in one block.
details: Every option is optional. A missing option is not checked at all. Vanilla mostly sets `imprisoned = no`, `incapable = no`, `adult = yes` and `alive = yes`.

fields.name: ai
fields.text: Whether the character is run by the AI (not a player).

fields.name: alive
fields.text: Whether the character is alive.

fields.name: female
fields.text: Whether the character is female.

fields.name: adult
fields.text: Whether the character is an adult.

fields.name: incapable
fields.text: Whether the character has any trait that makes them incapable.

fields.name: imprisoned
fields.text: Whether the character is in prison.

fields.name: hostage
fields.text: Whether the character is a hostage.

fields.name: travel
fields.text: Whether the character is travelling.

fields.name: activity
fields.text: Whether the character is in an activity.

fields.name: ruler
fields.text: Whether the character is a ruler.

fields.name: advanced_ruler
fields.text: Whether the character is a ruler with full access to the game's mechanics. Barons, rebels, mercenary leaders and holy order leaders do not pass this check.

fields.name: landed
fields.text: Whether the character holds land.

fields.name: in_army
fields.text: Whether the character is a commander or knight in an army on the map.

fields.name: at_war
fields.text: Whether the character is at war.

label: Is away from court
summary: Whether the character is away from the court.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it. Write `yes` to require it.

label: Is bad nickname
summary: Whether the given nickname is a bad one.
details: The game does not list which nicknames are bad. Vanilla uses it once, with a nickname passed in as a parameter.

label: Is barter army
summary: Whether the army is a barter army.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it. Write `yes` to require it.

label: Is betrothed
summary: Whether the character is betrothed (engaged to be married).
details: Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Bloc leader or heir of
summary: Whether the character is the leader of the given character's bloc, or the leader's player heir.
details: The other character is written as the value. The game does not explain the term bloc further, and vanilla does not use this trigger.

label: Travel is cancelled
summary: Whether the travel plan was cancelled.
details: A cancelled plan was stopped by hand and the traveller is sent back home. It runs on a travel plan.

label: Candidate from set
summary: Whether the character is a candidate for an elected title because of a given candidate set.
details: A character can qualify through several sets. The check looks at the first one in order of definition. It fails if the character is not a candidate for the title, or the title does not use election laws.

fields.name: title
fields.text: The title being elected.

fields.name: source
fields.text: The name of the candidate set the candidacy must come from.

label: Is capital barony
summary: Whether the title is a capital barony.
details: Runs on a title. Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Causing raid hostility toward
summary: Whether the character has made the given character hostile by raiding their realm.
details: The other character is written as the value, for example `prev` or `scope:host`. The game's documentation says the raiding of their top liege's (the highest ruler above them) realm also counts.

label: Interaction may be accepted
summary: Whether the given interaction is available from the character to the recipient and could be accepted by them.
details: Only `recipient` and `interaction` are always given in vanilla; the other fields are optional.

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: The character the interaction is aimed at.

fields.name: interaction
fields.text: The interaction to check.

fields.name: secondary_actor
fields.text: An optional extra character on the acting side (vanilla passes a hostage here).

fields.name: secondary_recipient
fields.text: An optional extra character on the receiving side (vanilla passes a hostage or a title holder here).

fields.name: target_title
fields.text: An optional title the interaction is about.

fields.name: required_response
fields.text: The kind of response required, `yes` or `maybe`.

fields.name: ai_accept
fields.text: The lowest acceptance value required.

label: Interaction is shown
summary: Whether the given interaction is shown from the character to the recipient.
details: It only checks that the interaction is shown, not that it can be used. `is_character_interaction_valid` checks both.

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: The character the interaction is aimed at.

fields.name: interaction
fields.text: The interaction to check.

label: Interaction is valid
summary: Whether the given interaction is both shown and usable from the character to the recipient.
details: It is stricter than `is_character_interaction_shown`, which only checks that it is shown.

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: The character the interaction is aimed at.

fields.name: interaction
fields.text: The interaction to check.

label: Main character of window
summary: Whether the local player is the main character of the character window.
details: It is an interface trigger and can only be used in specific places. Vanilla scripts do not use it.

label: Child of
summary: Whether the character is a child of the given character.
details: The parent is written as the value, for example `root` or `scope:liege`.

label: Is civil war
summary: Whether the war is a civil war.
details: Runs on a war. Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Is claimant
summary: Whether the character has a claim on any landed title.
details: Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Is clergy
summary: Whether the character is a member of the clergy.
details: Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Close family of
summary: Whether the character is close family of the given character.
details: Close family means parents, children, siblings, grandparents and grandchildren. The other character is written as the value, for example `root`.

label: Close or extended family of
summary: Whether the character is close or extended family of the given character.
details: This covers parents, children, siblings, grandparents and grandchildren, plus cousins, uncles, aunts, nephews and nieces. The other character is written as the value, for example `root`.

label: Coastal province
summary: Whether the province lies next to the sea.
details: Lakes do not count. Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Coastal county
summary: Whether the county lies next to the sea.
details: Lakes do not count. Runs on a title. Write `yes` to require it, `no` to require the opposite.

label: Combat side is attacker
summary: Whether this side of the combat was the attacker.
details: Runs on a combat side. Write `yes` to require the attacking side, `no` for the defending side.

label: Combat side is pursuing
summary: Whether this combat side is pursuing, which the game's documentation describes as being the winner of the combat.
details: The name says pursuing, the game's documentation says winner, and vanilla does not use it, so the exact meaning is not confirmed. Runs on a combat side.
